chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: His mother's career in Chicago and New York, sacrificed for her children
summary: His mother made a name in Chicago and New York but returned to get her two children from their grandparents.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So any way, she married and after they freed them, I think when Sherman marched through the South they freed the slaves, and she married, you know, my grandfather and had quite a few children. But the one that was most musical was my mother. And she went to -- my mother was in Chicago during the time that King Oliver was there, but I was still in Montgomery with my grandmother. So she came back and she -- as I told you she taught music and at Selma, at Paine College there. And I went to Selma with her. This is where she formed this band. But we left, luckily. We got out in time.

So that's really how it -- I started, you know. And through her I was exposed to just about everything. Because when she was in Chicago, evidently she made quite a name for herself, and then she was in New York, she made quite a name for herself there. But she sacrificed most of it because of her children. She had two to. We were with our grandparents. So she couldn't leave us there, she had to come back and forfeit that, you know, to come back and get us.
